The variable $z$ is being *divided* by $6.$ To isolate $z$ and remove the negative sign, we *multiply* by $-6$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\,\, & <\,\,-\frac{z}{6} \\ (-6)\cdot 4\,\, & >\,\,(-6)\cdot (-\frac{z}{6}) \\ -24\,\, & >\,\,(-6)\cdot (-\frac{z}{6})\end{aligned}
$$

Since two negative numbers multiply to give a positive number, we first cancel the negatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}-24\,\, & >(-6)\cdot (-\frac{z}{6}) \\ -24 & >(\cancel{-}6)\cdot (\cancel{-}\frac{z}{6}) \\ -24 & >6\cdot \frac{z}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $6$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}-24 & >6\cdot \frac{z}{6} \\ -24 & >\frac{6z}{6} \\ -24 & >\frac{\cancel{6}z}{\cancel{6}} \\ -24 & >z\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the inequality with the variable on the left-hand side:

$$
z<-24
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z<-24.$
